===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|flag}}, {{m|enm|flagge||flag}}, further etymology {{unc|en|nocap=1}}. Perhaps from or related to early {{der|en|enm|flage}} {{gloss|name for a baby's garment}} and {{der|en|ang|flagg}}, {{m|ang|flacg||[[cataplasm]], [[poultice]], [[plaster]]}}.  Or, perhaps ultimately {{onomatopoeic|en|title=imitative}}, or otherwise drawn from {{der|en|gem-pro|*flaką|t=something flat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-||flat, broad, plain}}, referring to the shape.<ref name = harper>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|flag}}</ref>

Germanic cognates include Saterland Frisian {{m|stq|Flaage||flag}}, West Frisian {{m|fy|flagge||flag}}, Dutch {{m|nl|vlag||flag}}, {{cog|de|Flagge||flag}}, {{cog|sv|flagga||flag}}, {{cog|da|flag||flag, ship's flag}}. Compare also {{cog|enm|flacken||to flutter, palpitate}}, {{cog|sv|-}} dialectal {{m|sv|flage||to flutter in the wind}}, {{cog|non|flögra||to flap about}}. Akin to {{cog|goh|flogarōn||to flutter}}, {{cog|goh|flogezen||to flutter, flicker}}, {{cog|enm|flakeren||to move quickly to and fro}}, {{cog|ang|flacor||fluttering, flying}}. More at {{l|en|flack}}, {{l|en|flacker}}.

[[Image:Hk5flagpole.JPG|right|thumb|Several [[flagpole]]s with flags]]

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{sid|en|Q14660}}{{lb|en|countable}} A piece of [[cloth]], often decorated with an [[emblem]], used as a visual [[signal]] or [[symbol]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|title=Burning EU and other flags can now bring German jail term|magazine=w:BBC|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52674809|date=2020-05-15|passage=The vote in the Bundestag (parliament) on Thursday makes defiling foreign '''flags''' equal to the crime of defiling the German '''flag'''. {{...}} The new law also applies to acts of defilement besides burning, such as publicly ripping a '''flag''' up.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250604073002/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52674809}}
# The [[design]] that could be placed on a flag, typically a [[rectangular]] [[graphic]] that is used to represent an [[entity]] (like a [[country]], [[organisation]] or group of people) or an [[idea]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''flag''' of France has three vertical stripes.}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} A flag flown by a [[ship]] to show the presence on board of the [[admiral]]; the admiral himself, or his flagship.
# {{lb|en|nautical|often used attributively}} A {{w|Flag signals|signal flag}}.
# The use of a flag, especially to indicate the start of a [[race]] or other event.
# {{lb|en|computer science}} A [[variable]] or memory location that [[store]]s a [[Boolean]] true-or-false, yes-or-no value, typically either recording the fact that a certain event has occurred or requesting that a certain optional action take place.
# {{lb|en|computer science}} In a [[CLI|command line interface]], a command parameter requesting optional behavior or otherwise modifying the action of the command being invoked.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author=Angel Sola Orbaiceta|title=Hardcore Programming for Mechanical Engineers|pages=19–2
|passage=This will be used as a help message if the user passes in the --help '''flag''', like so: {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|aviation}} A mechanical indicator that pops up to draw the pilot's attention to a problem or malfunction.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1966|author=Barry J. Schiff|title=All about Flying: An Introduction to the World of Flying|page=72
|passage=I was shooting an IFR approach down the San Francisco slot, when all of a sudden the ILS '''flag''' popped up.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1980|author=Paul Garrison|title=Flying VFR in marginal weather|page=139
|passage={{...}} and then the OFF '''flag''' popped up and the needle went dead.}}
# {{lb|en|British|uncountable}} The game of [[capture the flag]].
# {{lb|en|geometry}} A sequence of [[face]]s of a given [[polytope]], one of each dimension up to that of the polytope (formally, though in practice not always explicitly, including the [[null]] face and the polytope itself), such that each face in the sequence is part of the next-higher dimension face.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1994|author=John Ratcliffe|title=Foundations of Hyperbolic Manifolds|url=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=kvTiBwAAQBAJ&pg=PA230&dq=%22flag%22%7C%22flags%22+polytope&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwiEtu_XuPfMAhUC3mMKHewGAuQQ6AEIcDAN#v=onepage&q=%22flag%22%7C%22flags%22%20polytope&f=false|page=230|passage=A '''''flag''''' of ''P'' is a sequence (''F<sub>0</sub>, F<sub>1</sub>, ..., F<sub>m</sub>'') of faces of ''P'' such that dim ''F<sub>i</sub>'' = ''i'' for each ''i'' and ''F<sub>i</sub>'' is a side of ''F''<sub>''i''+1</sub> for each ''i'' < ''m''.{{...}}A ''regular polytope'' in ''X'' is a polytope ''P'' in ''X'' whose group of symmetries in <''P''> acts transitively on its '''flags'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Peter McMullen; Egon Schulte|title=Abstract Regular Polytopes|publisher=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Its Applications 92|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=JfmlMYe6MJgC&pg=PA31&dq=%22flag%22%7C%22flags%22+polytope&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwiEtu_XuPfMAhUC3mMKHewGAuQQ6AEIKjAA#v=onepage&q=%22flag%22%7C%22flags%22%20polytope&f=false|page=31
|passage=We call ''P'' (''combinatorially'') ''regular'' if its automorphism group ''Γ''(''P'') is transitive on its '''flags'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Peter McMullen; Egon Schulte|chapter=Regular and Chiral Polytopes in Low Dimensions|editors=Harold Scott Macdonald Coxeter; Chandler Davis; Erich W. Ellers|title=The Coxeter Legacy: Reflections and Projections|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=cKpBGcqpspIC&pg=PA91&dq=%22flag%22%7C%22flags%22+polytope&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwiEtu_XuPfMAhUC3mMKHewGAuQQ6AEIazAM#v=onepage&q=%22flag%22%7C%22flags%22%20polytope&f=false|page=91
|passage=Roughly speaking, chiral polytopes have half as many possible automorphisms as have regular polytopes. More technically, the ''n''-polytope ''P'' is ''chiral'' if it has two orbits of '''flags''' under its group ''Γ''(''P''), with adjacent '''flags''' in different orbits.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics|linear algebra}} A sequence of [[subspace]]s of a [[vector space]], beginning with the [[null]] space and ending with the vector space itself, such that each member of the sequence (until the last) is a [[proper]] subspace of the next.
# {{lb|en|television}} A dark piece of material that can be mounted on a stand to block or shape the light.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Des Lyver; Graham Swainson|title=Basics of Video Lighting|page=103
|passage=At the other extreme, with limitless budgets all they have to do is dream up amazing lighting rigs to be constructed and operated by the huge team of gaffers and sparks, with their generators, discharge lights, '''flags''', gobos and brutes.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=John Jackman|title=Lighting for Digital Video and Television|page=86
|passage='''Flags''' and other cutters allow the DP or gaffer to throw large controlled shadows on parts of the scene.}}
# {{lb|en|UK|archaic|slang}} An [[apron]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1887|author=William Ernest Henley|title=Villon's Straight Tip to All Cross Coves
|passage=Suppose you try a different tack, / And on the square you flash your '''flag'''?}}
# {{lb|en|internet slang|ACG}} An indication that a certain [[outcome]] or [[event]] is going to happen,  [[deduce|deduced]] not [[logically]] or [[causally]], but as a [[pattern]] in a piece of [[media]]. Chiefly used in [[video game]]s and adjacent media, especially [[visual novel]]s, it is typically described as being [[raised]] or [[set]] by the [[plot]] or [[words]] of a [[character]].
#: {{ux|en|set a death '''flag'''}}
#: {{ux|en|raise the heroine's '''flags''' (in a [[galge]])}}
# {{lb|en|UK|slang|obsolete}} A [[groat]]; [[fourpence]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1851|year_published=1861|author=w:Henry Mayhew
|title=w:London Labour and the London Poor
|passage={{...}} the orator pulled out a tremendous black doll, bought for a ‘'''flag'''’ (fourpence) of a retired rag-merchant, and dressed up in Oriental style.}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To furnish or deck out with flags.
# To [[mark]] with a flag, especially to indicate the importance of something.
#* {{quote-journal|en
|date=January 8, 2011
|author=Chris Bevan
|title=Arsenal 1 - 1 Leeds
|work=BBC
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9341711.stm
|page=
|passage={{w|Theo Walcott|Walcott}} was, briefly, awarded a penalty when he was upended in the box but referee {{w|Phil Dowd}} reversed his decision because {{w|Nicklas Bendtner|Bendtner}} had been '''flagged''' offside.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823102940/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9341711.stm|archivedate=23 August 2026}}
# {{lb|en|often with ''down''}} To [[signal]] to, especially to stop a passing vehicle etc.
#: {{ux|en|Please '''flag''' down a taxi for me.}}
# To convey (a message) by means of flag signals.
#: {{ux|en|to '''flag''' an order to troops or vessels at a distance}}
# {{lb|en|often with ''up''}} To note, mark or point out for attention.
#: {{ux|en|I've '''flagged''' up the need for further investigation into this.}}
#: {{ux|en|Users of the Internet forum can '''flag''' others' posts as inappropriate.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} To signal (an event).
#: {{ux|en|The compiler '''flagged''' three errors.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} To set a program variable to ''true''.
#: {{ux|en|'''Flag''' the debug option before running the program.}}
# To [[decoy]] ([[game]]) by waving a flag, handkerchief, etc. to arouse the animal's curiosity.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1885|author=w:Theodore Roosevelt|title=Hunting Trips of a Ranchman
|passage=This method of hunting, however, is not so much practised now as formerly, as the antelope are getting continually shyer and more difficult to '''flag'''.}}
# {{lb|en|sports}} To [[penalize]] for an [[infraction]].
#: {{ux|en|The defender was '''flagged''' for unsportsmanlike conduct.}}
# {{lb|en|chess|intransitive}} To lose on [[time]], especially in a [[blitz]] game; when using a traditional [[analog]] [[chess clock]], a flag would fall when time expired.
#* {{cite-book|passage=Indeed, I usually spent an hour to an hour and a half on my game, never found myself in time pressure, never once '''flagged''' in my entire life, except in blitz games, of course.|title=For Friends & Colleagues|volume=1|author=Mark Dvoretsky|year=2014|isbn= 1941270107}}
# {{lb|en|chess|transitive}} To defeat (an opponent) on [[time]], especially in a [[blitz]] game.
#: {{ux|en|White was winning positionally, but Black managed to '''flag''' him and win.}}
# {{lb|en|firearms}} To point the muzzle of a firearm at a person or object one does not intend to fire on.
# To fail, such as a class or an exam.
#: {{ux|en|After he '''flagged''' Algebra, Mike was ineligible for the football team.}}
# {{lb|en|biology}} In female canids, to signal mating readiness by moving the tail aside to expose the vulva.
#* {{quote-web|en|url=https://research.bangor.ac.uk/portal/files/7472365/PDB3357-00.pdf
|title=Life and Behaviour of Wolves|author=Pete Haswell|date=01/03/2011|text=She will avert her tail to the side ('''flagging'''), standing still when the male mounts.|work=Wolf Print|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108225519/https://research.bangor.ac.uk/portal/files/7472365/PDB3357-00.pdf|archivedate=8 January 2025}}

===Etymology 2===
Perhaps from a variant of {{m|en|flack||to hang loose}}, from {{der|en|enm|flacken}}; or perhaps from {{der|en|non|-}}.<ref name = harper>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|flag}}</ref> Compare {{cog|dum|flaggheren}}, {{m|dum|vlaggheren||to droop, flag}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[weaken]], become feeble.
#: {{ux|en|His strength '''flagged''' toward the end of the race.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1724|author=w:Jonathan Swift|chapter=w:Drapier's Letters|title=[[s:The Works of the Rev. Jonathan Swift/Volume 9/The Drapier’s Letters 2|2]]
|passage=He now sees a spirit has been raised against him, and he only watches till it begin to '''flag'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=December 29, 2012|author=Paul Doyle| title=Arsenal's {{w|Theo Walcott}} hits hat-trick in thrilling victory over Newcastle| url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2012/dec/29/arsenal-newcastle-united-premier-league| passage=The sides took it in turns to err and excite before {{w|Newcastle United FC|Newcastle}} '''flagged''' and {{w|Arsenal FC|Arsenal}} signalled their top-four credentials by blowing the visitors away.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013073237/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/dec/29/arsenal-newcastle-united-premier-league|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
# To hang loose without stiffness; to bend down, as flexible bodies; to be loose, yielding, limp.
#* {{RQ:Moore Lalla Rookh|passage=as loose it [the sail] '''flagged''' around the mast}}
# To let droop; to suffer to fall, or let fall, into feebleness.
#* {{RQ:Prior Poems|An Ode|passage=The Thousand Loves , that arm thy potent Eye , Must drop their Quivers , '''flag''' their Wings}}
# To [[enervate]]; to exhaust the vigour or elasticity of.

From {{inh|en|enm|flagge}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin, perhaps from {{der|en|gmq|-}}; compare {{cog|da|flæg|t=yellow iris}}.  Or, possibly from {{m|en|flag#Etymology_1|sense 1}}, referring to its motion in the wind. Compare also {{cog|nl|vlag}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# Any of various plants with sword-shaped [[leaf|leaves]], especially [[iris]]es; specifically, {{taxfmt|Iris pseudacorus|species}}.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Antony and Cleopatra|I|3|text=[T]he ebbed man, ne'er loved till ne'er worth love,<br>Comes deared by being lacked. This common body,<br>Like to a vagabond '''flag''' upon the stream,<br>Goes to and back, lackeying the varying tide,<br>To rot itself with motion.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Job|8|11|text=Can the rush grow up without mire? can the '''flag''' grow without water?}}
